assets.generationPrompt:
Create ONE entirely new current-world photorealistic travel-guide architectural photograph of the REAL BAHRAIN WORLD TRADE CENTER in MANAMA, Bahrain. Landscape native 1536 x 1024 pixels, 3:2, opaque RGB sRGB PNG.

Use the TWO actual independent photos for the SAME twin building: first B.alotaby (2016) front/seaward blue-hour view, second Francisco Anzola (2016) oblique street view. Study the authentic paired proportions from both. TWO slender mirrored angular SAIL-SHAPED silver/blue-glass towers rise to sharp pointed tips. Their inner faces form the tall central gap; their outer sloping sail faces taper to the point with clear horizontal floor bands and real pale structural edges. EXACTLY THREE horizontal connecting SKYBRIDGES cross the lower-to-middle part of the central gap, at the three photographed heights. Each bridge supports ONE real white three-bladed wind turbine centred in the gap, blades and hub facing toward the seaward camera. Thus three bridges and three turbines total, physically joined to both towers, aligned correctly in one gap. Preserve exact relative tower width/height and gap proportions from the photographs. Do not add a fourth bridge or turbine. Do not merge the two towers, turn them into pyramids, increase their thickness, substitute Dubai buildings, invent a top connecting roof, antenna mast or curved fantasy tower.

CAMERA: a fresh LOW ELEVATED ROOFTOP / landmark midpoint perspective, lens roughly level with the upper turbine bridge, well above the adjacent low roofs and streets but much lower than the pointed tower tips. Slightly oblique FRONT/SEAWARD view, chosen so all THREE turbine faces are clearly visible between the towers. Camera tilted gently DOWN about15 degrees toward the site: nearby low roof tops, the base approach and the ground directly below show from above. NOT a water-level horizontal/upward skyline snapshot, not street-level looking up, and NOT a high-altitude aerial. Natural professional full-frame architectural perspective, near verticals and moderate telephoto. BOTH whole tower silhouettes and pointed tips inside frame with breathing room; tall towers large and dominant across almost the full image height.

SCOPED AUTHENTIC SETTING: frame tightly around these actual twin towers and their immediately adjoining base/podium, a small strip of the seaward-side road/palms and understated low roof tops; use atmospheric haze and blue-hour shadow beyond that. Do NOT reproduce the 2016 wide skyline as today's skyline, do NOT invent recognisable new skyscrapers, clone the old Sheraton hotel facade or place ocean behind an inland-facing view. Avoid a broad metropolitan panorama. The main subject and the real three turbine bridges should be overwhelmingly dominant and easy to count even at small image size. Any remote background is unobtrusive soft haze and unidentifiable low urban texture, not a detailed skyline.

LIGHT: beautiful realistic early blue hour, deep but readable blue sky, restrained blue light accents along the tower edges and soft warm interior windows and street lights, correct glass reflections. Natural crisp architecture, believable depth, authentic materials and sophisticated professional documentary photography, not neon fantasy/HDR/illustration. The lighting is an artistic time choice, not a statement about the exact present light programme.

Do NOT copy source Instagram/Twitter credit, street billboards, hotel names, captions, signs, lettering, logos, number plates, flags, faces or people. No readable text of any kind, watermark, timestamp, border, UI, frame or collage. Make one whole new photo from the real reference geometry. Native 1536x1024 opaque sRGB PNG.

No readable source billboards, hotel lettering, Instagram watermark, faces, frame or logo. Two independent actual category/API-verified 2016 photos used for tower geometry only. Current operator confirms same sail-shaped tower/turbine identity. Blue-hour lights, low generic podium/urban context and soft background are illustrative; not an exact 2026 inventory, tower-light programme or city skyline survey.
